heading: Modelling built on first-principle physics, run at production scale.
lead: Every model we deliver traces back to the governing equations of multiphase, multicomponent flow in porous and fractured rock — not a black box. We calibrate against field observations, then push the model through HPC-scale ensembles to quantify what we don't yet know.

pipeline.heading: From digital model to resource assessment.

steps.title: Digital Model
steps.description: 3D geological model in Leapfrog — lithology, structure, clay-cap and fault geometry, built from surface geology, well data and geophysics.

steps.title: Reservoir Model
steps.description: The geological model discretised into a numerical simulation mesh, with rock properties assigned per unit.

steps.title: Natural-State Matching
steps.description: Calibrated against observed pressure, temperature and chemistry until the unperturbed model matches the real field.

steps.title: Uncertainty Quantification
steps.description: An ensemble of accepted natural-state realisations spanning the plausible parameter space, not a single best-fit model.

steps.title: Resource Assessment
steps.description: Automated well siting, pump sizing and production forecasting across the full ensemble — P10/P50/P90 output, not a point estimate.

capabilities.title: Numerical reservoir modelling
capabilities.description: Finite-volume, integral-finite-difference simulation of non-isothermal multiphase flow — natural-state calibration through decades-long production forecasting, in both single-porosity and fractured dual-porosity formulations.

capabilities.title: Parallel computing
capabilities.description: Production and exploration models are run as MPI-parallel ensembles across NeSI, AWS and Azure HPC infrastructure, turning multi-day single runs into same-day scenario comparisons.

capabilities.title: Uncertainty quantification
capabilities.description: Permeability, porosity and boundary conditions are treated as distributions, not point estimates — ensemble and history-matching methods translate geological uncertainty into a defensible resource-risk range.

capabilities.title: Software & tools
capabilities.description: Waiwera and TOUGH2 for the core physics, run through the Geothermal Modelling Framework (GMF) developed by O'Sullivan et al. (2023) for mesh generation, automated calibration, and post-processing.

items.title: Two-tier pump sizing under gas-breakout pressure (GBOP)
items.description: For CO2-bearing geothermal fluid, dissolved gas comes out of solution before the fluid reaches its own boiling point — a water-only NPSH threshold under-protects the pump. We size to GBOP (saturation pressure plus the fluid's own NCG partial pressure) plus a fixed safety margin, evaluated automatically for every candidate well, then matched against a real vendor pump catalogue — line-shaft or electric submersible, up to 30 stages — for a buildable specification and its parasitic shaft power.
items.figcap: Fig. — Electric submersible pump (ESP) completion, sized against the GBOP threshold.
items.alt: Electric submersible pump completion schematic with gas-breakout pressure and water-only NPSH thresholds vs. pump setting depth

items.title: Solving the wellbore as a transient problem
items.description: Most wellbore models treat the well as a quasi-steady-state pipe and solve the reservoir separately. Our wellbore modelling service uses a genuinely transient, multi-feed formulation — developed with our academic advisor Ryan Tonkin at the University of Auckland — that solves two-phase flow, counter-flow between feedzones, and start-up/shut-in behaviour as they evolve in time, then matches the result directly against measured downhole temperature, pressure and enthalpy logs rather than a single steady-state snapshot.

items.alt: Animated transient wellbore simulation for well AZ-18, showing simulated temperature, pressure and liquid-enthalpy profiles converging toward measured field data as the solver iterates, alongside the well's radial mesh
